title: act-on-weather / Service health
description: Is the stack answering, and how well. Hand-written rather than exported, so it stays readable as a file. Every panel uses a core Grafana visualisation (timeseries, stat, table) -- no plugin panels, because a plugin is something Grafana would have to download from grafana.com and this stack has no route out.

panels.title: Firing alerts (there is no Alertmanager -- this panel is the delivery path)
panels.description: ALERTS is the series Prometheus writes for every rule it is evaluating. This stack ships no Alertmanager on purpose: an air-gapped single host has no mail relay and no webhook target, so a routing component would have nowhere to route. observability/prometheus/alerts.yml gives the full argument, and every rule's description says what to do about it. An empty table here is the healthy state.

panels.title: Scrape targets -- 1 is up, 0 is unreachable
panels.description: Written by Prometheus itself, not by the services, so a container that is crash-looping before it can serve a single metric still shows here as 0. That is the difference between 'the service reports a problem' and 'the service is gone', and only the second one is visible in this panel.

panels.title: Application services currently reachable (of 5)
panels.description: api, agent, ingestor, consumer, enricher. Anything below 5 means AowServiceDown is either firing or about to: the rule allows two minutes of absence before it fires, so this panel moves first.

panels.title: Local model server
panels.description: Deliberately separate from the count beside it, because the model being down is NOT a pipeline outage. The enricher polls pending recommendations instead of sitting in the ingest path, so weather is fetched, published and stored exactly as normal while this reads 0; what changes is that recommendations stay 'pending' until `make reenrich` catches them up.

panels.title: HTTP request rate by service and route (requests/second)
panels.description: route is the FastAPI route TEMPLATE -- /weather/{city}, not /weather/Rome -- so five cities are one series rather than five. Anything that matched no route at all is reported as <unmatched>, which is usually a scanner or a typo rather than a bug.

panels.title: Server-error ratio by service and route (share of requests returning 5xx)
panels.description: 5xx responses divided by requests for each active route. A route with traffic and no 5xx shows 0%; a route with no requests in the five-minute window has no ratio. Unhandled exceptions are counted as 500 responses. AowServerErrors fires above 5% sustained for ten minutes.

targets.expr: (sum by (service, route) (rate(aow_http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum by (service, route) (rate(aow_http_requests_total[5m]))) or (0 * (sum by (service, route) (rate(aow_http_requests_total[5m])) > 0))

panels.title: Request duration p50 (typical request, seconds)
panels.description: The median, from the aow_http_request_duration_seconds histogram. Read it next to the p95 panel: p50 flat while p95 climbs means a slow tail (one endpoint, or contention on the model server); both climbing together means the whole host is loaded.

panels.title: Request duration p95 (slow tail, seconds) -- AowHighLatency fires above 5s
panels.description: What a user actually waits for. The agent's chat route is expected to sit high on a CPU-only host: a 1.7B model generating a grounded answer is seconds, not milliseconds. The 5s threshold on AowHighLatency was chosen above that normal cost so a healthy answer does not page anyone.

panels.title: Unhandled exceptions since service start, by class
panels.description: Cumulative exceptions recorded by each running service, grouped by route and class. An empty table means no unhandled exceptions since the current processes started. A nonzero row can be historical; compare it with the 5xx ratio to see whether errors are happening now.
